title: Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations
hook: OpenAI told the field to switch to SWE-Bench Pro after finding SWE-bench Verified contaminated. Now its own audit says ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro's tasks are broken too.
key_points: OpenAI previously found contamination and design flaws in SWE-bench Verified and recommended the community move to SWE-Bench Pro instead.
A fresh audit — automated review plus checks by five experienced engineers — flagged roughly 30% of SWE-Bench Pro's tasks as broken.
OpenAI is retracting its own recommendation, saying the benchmark no longer reliably measures frontier coding capability.
Reported pass rates on SWE-Bench Pro climbed from 23.3% to 80.3% in eight months — a jump OpenAI blames partly on benchmark noise.
The episode shows how fast a widely-adopted coding benchmark can decay once models start being optimized against it.
content_html: OpenAI just retracted its own advice. Months after telling the field to trade SWE-bench Verified for SWE-Bench Pro — a fix for contamination it had found in the older benchmark — an internal audit found that roughly 30% of SWE-Bench Pro's own tasks are broken.
extra_html:
The audit combined an automated pipeline — reviewing model attempts, task metadata, and failure traces — with independent checks from five experienced software engineers, to separate genuinely broken tasks from ones that are merely hard. Reported pass rates on the benchmark had climbed from 23.3% to 80.3% over roughly eight months, a rise OpenAI says reflects the benchmark hitting a noise ceiling rather than a leap in real capability of that size.

The reversal is a reminder that coding benchmarks decay fast once they become the target everyone optimizes against — even a benchmark the field's top lab endorsed months earlier can turn out to be quietly broken underneath its own leaderboard. OpenAI, July 2026.

flashcards.prompt: What happened to frontier model pass rates on SWE-Bench Pro over about eight months?

choices.text: They dropped as newer models were tested

flashcards.explanation_html: OpenAI says a rise that steep signals the benchmark is saturating and noisy, not that models alone improved by that much.
